faqs.q: What is the best automatic litter box in 2026?
faqs.a: It depends on where you can install it. Litter-Robot 5 is listed 'As low as $799' and only needs a wall outlet, so it fits anywhere; CatGenie Whoosh is $469.00 but needs a one-time hook-up to cold water and a laundry drainpipe or toilet; PETKIT's Purobot Max 3 is $399.99 against a $499.99 regular price with no plumbing printed; and Meowant's MW-SC02 is $399.99 against $559.99. All four prices were read from the brands' own pages on 2026-09-27.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest automatic litter box on this list?
faqs.a: PETKIT's catalog is the lowest printed today: the Purobot Crystal Duo is $199.99 against a $299.99 regular price, and the Purobot Max 3 is $399.99 against $499.99. Meowant's MW-SC02 matches that $399.99 figure against a $559.99 regular price, while Litter-Robot 5 is listed 'As low as $799' and CatGenie Whoosh at $469.00.

faqs.q: Does the CatGenie need plumbing?
faqs.a: Yes. The CatGenie units page states a one-time hook-up to cold water, a laundry drainpipe or toilet, electricity and Wi-Fi, and says the unit is normally installed in the laundry room, bathroom or utility room. It ships with T-Adapters for that setup, and the FAQ adds that the Whoosh model is safe for septic systems.

faqs.q: What litter can I use in a Litter-Robot?
faqs.a: Whisker's FAQ says the best litter is a high-quality, standard-weight clay-based clumping litter such as GreatLitter. Some silica gel beads and crystals work if they pass through the screen, but translucent or white litter can affect litter level and Drawer Full Indicator accuracy, and plant-based, non-clumping, newspaper-based and wood pellet litters do not work.

faqs.q: How often do you empty an automatic litter box?
faqs.a: The official FAQ says a Litter-Robot 5 drawer may only need emptying once every 10 days in a one-cat household, Litter-Robot 4 once every 8 days and Litter-Robot EVO about once a week, with a full-drawer notification. Meowant's SC09 page says its 6.7L bin goes up to 14 days, and PETKIT's collection claims 15 to 30 days depending on the model.

faqs.q: Do these automatic litter boxes need a subscription?
faqs.a: None of the four prints a required monthly plan on the product pages checked. The paid extras are optional: PETKIT says you can upgrade to PETKIT Care+ for 30-day video history, and Litter-Robot offers a Whisker+ membership for longer history in the app. The consumables you do re-buy are litter, liners and - on CatGenie - a SaniSolution cartridge at $25.99.

faqs.q: How long do I have to return an automatic litter box?
faqs.a: It differs by seller. PETKIT's policy allows a return request within thirty (30) calendar days of delivery for eligible items. CatGenie gives 90 days with a return authorization and the unit arriving within 10 days of that authorization, Litter-Robot advertises a 90-day in-home trial where you pay return shipping, and Meowant prints a 90-Day Free Trial on the SC09 and a 30-Day Free Trial on the SC02.

faqs.q: Is the CatGenie Whoosh different from the CatGenie A.I.?
faqs.a: Yes. Whoosh uses the brand's disposable, plumbing-safe, water-soluble plant-derived litter and clumps liquids in the bowl; A.I. uses reusable washable granules that are washed and dried rather than replaced. The units page prices Whoosh at $469.00 (regular $499.00) and A.I. at $499.00 (regular $529.00), and both include an 18-month warranty and lifetime app access.

faqs.q: Which of these handles the biggest cats?
faqs.a: Two publish a 30 lb ceiling: Litter-Robot 5 takes cats from 3 to 30 lb and up to 5 cats, and Meowant's SC09 takes 3.3 to 30 lb with a 106L toilet area and an 8 in entrance. PETKIT's Max 3, Max Pro 2 and Ultra stop at 22 lb, while the CatGenie FAQ says there is no weight limit but recommends 1-3 cats up to 20 lb for the Whoosh.

faqs.q: Can I pay for an automatic litter box over time?
faqs.a: Whisker's financing page offers 0% APR through Affirm on eligible purchases with plans of 3, 6, 12 or 18 months, and notes that only products in the pay-over-time category qualify and that approval is Affirm's. The Litter-Robot 5 page separately offers HSA/FSA eligibility through Flex with approval within 24 hours.

blocks.h2: How this page was checked
blocks.html:
On 2026-09-27 (UTC+8) we opened four official stores in plain HTML and read what each one prints: litter-robot.com's Litter-Robot 5 product page, its FAQ and its payment-options page; catgenie.com's CatGenie units page, its returns page and its FAQ; petkit.com's automatic litter box collection, the Purobot Max 3 page, the cat-litter collection and the shipping, warranty and return policies; and meowant.com's SC09, SC02 and liners product pages. Every number in the table below was on one of those pages on that date, with its own source link.

The finding worth keeping: these four do not sell the same way. One prices itself 'as low as', three print a sale price next to a regular price, one of the four flushes its waste through your plumbing while the other three store it in a drawer you empty yourself, and the return windows run 30 or 90 days depending on the seller. That combination - not a review score - is what decides the purchase.

blocks.h2: What the answer comes down to
blocks.html:
If you want the lowest published price, PETKIT's catalog floors at $199.99 for the Purobot Crystal Duo and $399.99 for the Max 3 (regular $499.99), and Meowant's SC02 sits at $399.99 against $559.99. Both are app-controlled boxes with no plumbing printed on the page.

If you want no plumbing at all, Litter-Robot plugs into the wall and empties into a drawer: the FAQ says a Litter-Robot 5 drawer may need emptying once every 10 days in a one-cat household, against once every 8 days for Litter-Robot 4, and it takes clumping clay litter only.

If you never want to touch waste, CatGenie is the only one of the four that flushes - it wants cold water and a laundry drainpipe or toilet, and it sells you its own litter system, either disposable Whoosh litter or reusable washable granules with a $25.99 SaniSolution cartridge.

On the try-it terms, Litter-Robot and CatGenie both print 90 days, Meowant prints 90 days on the SC09 and 30 days on the SC02, and PETKIT's policy allows 30 calendar days from delivery. Every one of them puts conditions on the refund - return shipping, a return authorization, a 20% handling charge or a restocking rule - so read the linked returns page before you order, not after.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest Litter-Robot alternative printed today?

faqs.q: Which is cheaper, Furbo or Petcube?
faqs.a: The cheapest camera each store prints on 2026-09-30: Petcube's Petcube Cam at $26.99 against $34.99, and Furbo's 360° dog and cat cameras at $54 against 'original price is $184'. Petcube's most expensive camera, the Bites 2 Lite, is $79.99 against $149.99. These are per-device prices in USD read from the two official stores; nothing here is subtracted from anything else.

faqs.q: Do I have to pay for a subscription with either brand?
faqs.a: No, on both sides. Furbo's FAQ says 'Furbo Nanny is an optional subscription plan ... if you purchase the camera only' and Petcube's FAQ says 'By default, there is no monthly fee unless you choose to subscribe to an optional Petcube Care video cloud recording plan.' What you give up without it differs: Furbo's alerts, recordings and daily recap sit behind Nanny, and Petcube's Basic tier lists live streaming but no video history.

faqs.q: How much do the two subscriptions cost?
faqs.a: Furbo publishes six Nanny rates: Standard $9.99/mo monthly, $6.99/mo yearly average, $6.49/mo on 2 years; Premium $12.49/mo monthly, $8.74/mo yearly, $8.12/mo on 2 years. Petcube publishes three Care tiers: Basic free, Optimal $9.99/mo monthly or $4.99/mo yearly average ($59.88 total), Premium $16.99/mo monthly or $11.99/mo yearly ($143.88 total). The yearly figures are site-printed averages - monthly billing on the same tier is higher - so the two columns are not the same kind of number.

faqs.q: Do both subscriptions come with a free trial?
faqs.a: Both print 14 days. Furbo: 'you may choose to purchase after your FREE 14-day trial'; Petcube: 'A 14-day free trial to Petcube Care is included with every Petcube camera purchase.' Furbo's header separately runs a 'FREE camera + 30 days of Furbo Nanny' promotion, which is a different offer from the trial.

faqs.q: Which one has the longer return window?
faqs.a: Petcube: 45 calendar days from the purchase date with an RMA requested from support@petcube.com. Furbo: 30 days - 'Free Returns within 30 Days' in the buy box and 'you will have 30 days to return or exchange your Furbo' in the FAQ.

faqs.q: Which camera tosses treats?
faqs.a: Furbo: both models - the spec block prints a 100-piece treat capacity and 0.4-inch treats, and the product title is 'Treat Tossing Pet Camera'. Petcube: the Bites 2 Lite, described as a 'Smart HD pet camera with treat dispenser'; the Cam 360 page read prints no dispenser.

faqs.q: Does Petcube really have no monthly fee?
faqs.a: For the cameras, yes - its own FAQ says there is no monthly fee by default. The GPS Tracker is the exception on the same site: 'Do I need a subscription to use it? Yes', with Basic from $12/mo monthly ($7/mo yearly) and Premium from $8/mo yearly, and it is a tracker rather than a camera.

faqs.q: Which warranty is longer?
faqs.a: As printed: Furbo gives 1 year on every purchase, and adds a lifetime hardware warranty on yearly and 2-year plans while the Furbo Nanny subscription stays active. Petcube's policy page gives 1 year in the US and Canada and 2 years in the EU and UK, product pages print 1-year limited, and its Care table grants 2-year warranty only on the Premium tier. Both brands tie the longer warranty to a subscription or a region - read the condition before counting on it.

faqs.q: Is shipping free?
faqs.a: Furbo prints 'Free US Shipping' in the buy box on both camera pages. Petcube prints no free-shipping threshold on the shipping policy page read, and its store FAQ says shipping depends on Standard, Expedited or Priority speed with prices varying by location and option.

faqs.q: Which camera sees more of the room?
faqs.a: As printed on 2026-09-30: Petcube's Cam 360 pairs a 105° wide-angle view with 360° pan-tilt and 8x zoom; the Bites 2 Lite prints a 160° lens. Furbo's dog camera prints a Rotating 360° View with 4x digital zoom, and the cat camera's spec block prints a 130° wide-angle lens while a feature card on the same page prints 132° (diagonal). These are each brand's own numbers, not a lab measurement, and are not ranked here.

Prices, banners, plan rates, stock and trial terms change without notice - check the linked page before you buy. Every figure is in USD as printed; we do not convert currencies or average across billing periods, and no figure on this page was taken from a comparison site.

blocks.h2: How this page was checked
blocks.html:
On 2026-09-30 (UTC+8) we opened both official stores and read what each one prints: furbo.com's Furbo 360° Dog Camera and Furbo 360° Cat Camera product pages - buy box, Furbo Nanny plan table, spec block and page FAQ - and petcube.com's Cam 360, Bites 2 Lite, Care plan table and GPS Tracker pages, plus its warranty and shipping-and-returns policy pages. Every number in the table below came off one of those pages on that date, with its own source link.

The findings worth keeping: both brands make the subscription optional and both print exactly a 14-day free trial (Furbo's FAQ and Petcube's Care table) - while Furbo's header simultaneously runs a separate 'FREE camera + 30 days of Furbo Nanny' offer, so one site shows two trial lengths for the same subscription. Both brands also make the longer warranty conditional: Furbo extends to a lifetime hardware warranty only while a yearly or 2-year Nanny plan is active, and Petcube's Care table grants 2-year only on Premium while its own policy page says 1 year for the US and Canada and 2 years for the EU and UK. On price, Furbo prints one camera design at $54 (was $184) on both model pages, while Petcube prints five devices from $26.99 - and on service levels Furbo prints 'Free US Shipping' in the buy box where Petcube's shipping FAQ only prints three delivery speeds with prices that 'vary depending on your location'.

blocks.h2: What the answer comes down to
blocks.html:
If price decides it, Petcube's menu floors at $26.99 for the Petcube Cam (was $34.99) and its 360° model is $34.99 (was $52.99); Furbo does not do tiers - the dog and the cat camera are the same $54 against 'original price is $184', and the default button on the page is 'Subscribe now - $137.92' because the yearly plan is pre-selected.

If the subscription decides it, Furbo sells two tiers across three billing periods (six published rates, $6.49 to $12.49 per month as printed) with a 3-day history on Standard, while Petcube keeps a free Basic tier, puts 3 days on Optimal and 90 days plus 24/7 Online Vet chat on Premium - and separately sells a camera bundle 'starting from $5.99/mo'. Both give you 14 free days first.

If the paperwork decides it, Petcube's 45 calendar days beat Furbo's 30 on returns, but Furbo prints 'Free US Shipping' where Petcube prints no threshold, and each brand dangles a longer warranty only while you stay subscribed (Furbo) or move to Premium (Petcube). Read the condition with the number.

If the room decides it, Furbo's dog camera rotates 360° with treat tossing built into both models, Petcube spreads the same money across a pan-tilt Cam 360, a treat-dispensing Bites 2 Lite and a cheap fixed Cam - and only Petcube also sells a GPS tracker, which is the one device in either catalog that cannot work without a paid plan.
